Taazour's AOUN verification platform was launched: beneficiaries in the social registry database received SMS messages with a link to the platform to verify eligibility, see their collection code and complete identity verification, targeting 2,057,006 registered citizens.

fact: Decree 2024-073 of 15 May 2024 makes every poor household enrolled in the Registre Social eligible for Tekavoul's regular transfers (articles 11) and every vulnerable enrolled household eligible for its shock-response transfers (article 13), so the programme's regular and Tekavoul Choc components both draw beneficiaries from the Registre Social.

The World Bank's March 2026 status report says Decree 2025-162 established a dedicated sub-registry for disaster-affected households within the national Social Registry, with full operationalisation with the Ministry of Interior and the World Bank expected by 31 December 2026.

Decree 2025-162 of 15 October 2025 creates the BDS-MAC disaster-household database, fed by Taazour's Registre Social data among other sources, with lists of affected households sent back to the Registre Social to update it as the targeting base for shock-response programmes; an arrete of the Interior Minister is still to set its operating rules.

The World Bank ISR reports 17 users with signed agreements with the Social Registry as of March 2025 (baseline 7 in July 2020), out of at least 25 governmental and non-governmental users, including Elmaouna, WFP, UNHCR and UNICEF, using it to select beneficiaries.

The World Bank ISR reports that, in a civil-registration pilot, the government signed a convention between the Social Registry and ANRPTS, the civil registry agency, with enrollment support under way.

The World Bank ICR says the government designed and implemented a consolidated MIS built on three interoperable systems, the Social Registry, Tekavoul and Elmaouna, whose structure links the registry and payment systems.

The World Bank ICR says the Social Registry was in use by 13 actors in 2020, including Tadamoun/Taazour, WFP, Oxfam, ACF, UNHCR and Save the Children, and that the Prime Minister announced in September 2019 that all social programmes would eventually have to use it for targeting.
